title: Factorization of the actual completed-pullback comparison through the limit mate
statement:
Let $g:Y\to X$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], with small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Fix a Noetherian adic datum $(A,I)$, $P_n=A/I^n$ for $n\ge1$, and $B_T=\varprojlim_n(P_n)_T$ for $T=X,Y$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Assume the projection-defined coefficient map $c_g:g^{-1}B_X\to B_Y$ of [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] is an isomorphism. Use module sheaves, their unbounded derived categories and strict inverse sequences [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-inverse-system].

Put $F(M)=g^{-1}M\otimes_{g^{-1}B_X,c_g}B_Y$, and assume $F$ is additive and exact. Let $F_D:D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_X))\to D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_Y))$ and $F_D^{\mathrm{Tow}}$ be exact termwise pullback, identified with the specified left-derived functors by their original universal counits as in [lem-sf-exact-pullback-counit-normalization]. Fix the canonical constant-tower/total-right-derived-limit adjunctions $\Delta_T\dashv L_T$, with unit $v_T$ and counit $\varepsilon_T$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit, lem-coef-derived-tower-counit-projections]. Let $j:F_D^{\mathrm{Tow}}\Delta_X\xrightarrow{\sim}\Delta_YF_D$ be the identification induced from equality on ordinary constant towers and those counit-normalized comparisons. For a derived strict tower $M$ define its right mate
$$\beta_M=L_Y(F_D^{\mathrm{Tow}}\varepsilon_{X,M})\,L_Y(j_{L_XM}^{-1})\,v_{Y,F_DL_XM}.$$
For $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_X))$ let $i_K:\Delta_XK\to K_\bullet$ be its strict quotient augmentation, and put $\operatorname{comp}_K=L_X(i_K)v_{X,K}$, with the quotient tower and unit of [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]. Denote by $\alpha^F_K:F_DK\to L_YF_D^{\mathrm{Tow}}K_\bullet$ the actual ambient ordinary-to-completed comparison after the counit-normalized identifications above.

The following identity holds naturally in every unbounded $K$:
$$\alpha^F_K=\beta_{K_\bullet}\,F_D(\operatorname{comp}_K).$$
Here $\alpha^F_K$ is the projection-defined K-injective/strict-augmentation map specified in [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback], rather than an arbitrary map to the limit object. If $p_n:L_YF_D^{\mathrm{Tow}}K_\bullet\to F_D(K_n)$ is its specified evaluation and $q_{n,K}:K\to K_n$ the quotient augmentation, then
$$p_n\alpha^F_K=F_D(q_{n,K}).$$
For every $m\ge n$, $F_D(\rho_{m,n})p_m=p_n$, where $\rho_{m,n}:K_m\to K_n$ is the strict quotient transition, and these identities respect composite quotient transitions. No completeness of $K$ or countable-product preservation by $F$ is assumed.

proof.text: Write $H=F_D$, $\widetilde H=F_D^{\mathrm{Tow}}$, $M=K_\bullet$ and $a_K=\widetilde H(i_K)j_K^{-1}$. Apply [lem-sf-completed-augmentation-adjunct] with the given exact pullback and its original counit normalization. It identifies the actual specified comparison, including the K-injective representative, as $\alpha^F_K=L_Y(a_K)v_{Y,HK}$, naturally in every unbounded $K$. proof.text:
Set $h=\operatorname{comp}_K:K\to L_XM$. Expand the definition of $\beta_M$ and move $H(h)$ past $v_Y$ by its naturality. Naturality of $j^{-1}$ for $h$ gives
$$\begin{aligned}
\beta_M H(h)
 &=L_Y\bigl(\widetilde H(\varepsilon_{X,M})j^{-1}_{L_XM}\Delta_YH(h)\bigr)v_{Y,HK}\\
 &=L_Y\bigl(\widetilde H(\varepsilon_{X,M}\Delta_Xh)j_K^{-1}\bigr)v_{Y,HK}.
\end{aligned}$$
The first move is $v_{Y,HL_XM}H(h)=L_Y\Delta_YH(h)v_{Y,HK}$, and the second is $j^{-1}_{L_XM}\Delta_YH(h)=\widetilde H(\Delta_Xh)j_K^{-1}$. These are substitutions of naturality and functoriality, with no preservation-of-limit assumption. This is formalized by the private generic adjunction lemma mate_augmentation, avoiding any unfolding of the concrete derived categories.

proof.text:
The source completion map is $h=L_X(i_K)v_{X,K}$. Counit naturality for $i_K:\Delta_XK\to M$ and the left triangle identity give
$$\begin{aligned}
\varepsilon_{X,M}\Delta_Xh
 &=\varepsilon_{X,M}\Delta_XL_X(i_K)\Delta_Xv_{X,K}\\
 &=i_K\varepsilon_{X,\Delta_XK}\Delta_Xv_{X,K}
 =i_K.
\end{aligned}$$
Substitution in Step 2 gives $\beta_M H(\operatorname{comp}_K)=L_Y(\widetilde H(i_K)j_K^{-1})v_{Y,HK}$, which equals $\alpha^F_K$ by Step 1. This is an equality of the actual morphisms in the derived category, obtained before evaluating any projection.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-exact-tower-augmented-counit-evaluation] to $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(B_X)$, $\mathcal B=\operatorname{Mod}(B_Y)$ and $i=i_K$. Its $b$ is $\alpha^F_K$ by Step 1; its normalized $q_n,p_n$ are the specified $q_{n,K},p_n$. It gives $p_n\alpha^F_K=H(q_{n,K})$ and $H(\rho_{m,n})p_m=p_n$, including the identity-index case. For $m\ge n\ge r$, the quotient law of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] and the inverse-system convention [def-weil-inverse-system] give $\rho_{n,r}\rho_{m,n}=\rho_{m,r}$, so the same theorem gives $H(\rho_{n,r})H(\rho_{m,n})p_m=H(\rho_{m,r})p_m=p_r$. Naturality follows from its commuting-pair formula with $u=(K\mapsto K_\bullet)(f)$ and the natural quotient augmentation. Steps 2–3 are equalities of morphisms before projection. No completeness of $K$ or product preservation by $F$ has entered. For the specified projection normalization, reuse the proved private helpers derivedCounit_unit and limitCounitProjection_eq from CompletedDirectImageLimits [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits]. The complex unit is the existing right-derived unit on the homotopy quotient. Its universal property follows from the K-injective derivability structure and completedRlim_computation; its canonical adjunction counit equation is derivedCounit_unit. The equality limitCounitProjection_eq identifies the actual published projection with evaluation of that same counit. Supply these as the normalization parameters of exact_tower_augmented_counit_evaluation. Its third, fourth and fifth conjuncts give the finite augmentation, transition, and composite-transition clauses. Expand the canonical comparison definitions; mapDerivedCategoryNatIso of the inverse comparison has inverse definitionally equal to mapDerivedCategoryNatIso of the forward comparison. This also handles equal indices. No hypotheses or definitions change.
